meaning: From ~ to ~ / over (a range or span of time or place)

exercises.example_sentence: 夕方から夜にかけて、気温が下がる。
exercises.translation: The temperature drops from evening to night.
wrong_choice_explanations: に比べて means 'compared with', but nothing is being compared here; the sentence describes the temperature falling over the evening-to-night span, which needs にかけて.
によって means 'depending on / by means of', which can't mark the evening-to-night span over which the temperature falls; にかけて is needed.
に対して means 'toward / in contrast to'; it can't close a から range to mark the evening-to-night span over which the temperature falls — that needs にかけて.

exercises.example_sentence: 年末から年始にかけて、多くの店が休む。
exercises.translation: Many stores close from the end of the year to the beginning of the new year.
wrong_choice_explanations: に比べて means 'compared with', but nothing is being compared — the sentence marks the span over which the closures run, which needs にかけて.
によって means 'by / depending on'; it can't close a から range to mark a time span.
から alone indicates a starting point, and 年末から年始から is ungrammatical; にかけて closes the range.

exercises.example_sentence: 今週から来週にかけて、出張の予定がある。
exercises.translation: I have business trips planned from this week to next week.
wrong_choice_explanations: のうちに means 'before next week is over,' marking a window to get something done, not the continuous this-week-to-next-week span that にかけて conveys.
を通して means 'throughout' an entire period, but this sentence needs にかけて to express the range from this week to next week.
までに indicates a deadline, but this sentence needs にかけて to express the period from this week to next week.

exercises.example_sentence: 来月から再来月にかけて、新商品の発売が続く。
exercises.translation: New product releases will continue from next month to the month after next.
wrong_choice_explanations: の間に pinpoints a moment within the span, which clashes with 続く ('continues'); にかけて expresses the ongoing run from next month into the month after.
を通じて means 'through/via' as a means, but this sentence needs にかけて to express the time span from next month to the month after.
から alone indicates starting point but doesn't express the range that にかけて provides from next month to the month after.

exercises.example_sentence: 春から夏にかけて、日がだんだん長くなる。
exercises.translation: From spring into summer, the days gradually get longer.
wrong_choice_explanations: に比べて means 'compared with'; the sentence describes a span of time, not a comparison.
によって means 'by / depending on'; it can't close a から range to mark a period.
に対して means 'toward / in contrast to'; it doesn't mark the end of a time span.

exercises.example_sentence: 朝から昼にかけて、この道は人が多くなる。

wrong_choice_explanations: に比べて means 'compared with'; nothing is being compared — the sentence marks a time span.
をはじめ means 'starting with' an example from a group; it can't close a から time range.
に対して means 'toward / in contrast to'; it doesn't mark the end of a time span.

exercises.example_sentence: 4月から5月にかけて桜が咲きます。
exercises.translation: Cherry blossoms bloom from April to May.
wrong_choice_explanations: に比べて means 'compared with'; 〜から〜に比べて is not a range expression. 〜から〜にかけて marks the span 'from … through …'.
によって means 'by / depending on'; it can't close a から range. にかけて marks the end of the span 'from … through …'.
に対して means 'toward / in contrast to'; it can't close a から range. にかけて marks the span 'from … through …'.
